title: Write-preferring read-write lock
prompt:
Implement a write-preferring readers-writer lock on top of one intrinsic monitor
(synchronized + wait/notifyAll). Solution has four instance methods:

  void lockRead()    void unlockRead()
  void lockWrite()   void unlockWrite()

Rules:
- Any number of readers may hold the lock at the same time.
- A writer holds it alone: no readers, no second writer.
- Write-preferring: once a writer is waiting for the lock, a reader that calls
  lockRead() after that must wait until the writer has acquired and released.
  (So you have to track how many writers are WAITING, not just the active one.)
- Every wait() belongs in a while loop - spurious wakeups are real.
- Use notifyAll(), not notify(): readers and writers wait on the same monitor.
- The thread that locks is the thread that unlocks; no reentrancy needed.

Keep the signatures exactly as given: no `throws` (handle InterruptedException
inside - the grader never interrupts these threads) and nothing `private`.
